newsitem.title: UK: Gottesman office silent on Olivetti plans.
newsitem.headline: Gottesman office silent on Olivetti plans.

text.p: The London legal office of U.S. financier Edward Gottesman stuck rigidly to its "no comment" stance on Monday as speculation gripped the Milan market that he was part of a group poised to buy Olivetti's troubled PC arm.

The Italian information technology group has had its shares suspended on the Milan stock exchange pending "an important announcement" that analysts expect to involve the sale of its loss-making personal computer business.
Gottesman's assistant at his legal firm Gottesman, Jones and Partners said only: "I'm afraid there is nothing I can add." She would not divulge the businessman's whereabouts.

Italian sources have said that Gottesman, who also heads venture capital firm Centenary group, has linked up a consortium of investors including the chairman of Electrolux unit Zanussi Gianmario Rossignolo, and has been in talks to buy the division.
Analysts are anxiously awaiting Olivetti's announcement, scheduled for 1600 GMT, to shed light on a price it may have clinched for the unit.

While newspaper reports have said the Gottesman consortium has agreed to pay 200 billion lire for the business, some analysts have also not ruled out the possibility that the ailing group is planning a more far-reaching restructuring.
